model_annotation: The plot illustrates how classification accuracy (ACC) varies with co-occurrence number for six methods (Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME). The x-axis is labeled “Co-occurrence Number” and uses a logarithmic scale, spanning from about 1 to about 3000, with major ticks shown at 0, 10, 100, and 1000. The y-axis is labeled “ACC (%)” on a linear scale, ranging roughly from 38% to 66%, with labeled ticks at 40, 45, 50, 55, 60, and 65. The Base series is a black solid line with circular markers, increasing from about 38% at the smallest co-occurrence value to about 42% near 30, then to about 44% around 300 and remaining about 44% at the largest value. FT is a blue solid line with downward-triangle markers, rising from about 40% to about 43% near 30, to about 46% around 300, and to about 48% at the largest value. IKE is a red solid line with upward-triangle markers, increasing from about 43% to about 45% near 30, to about 46.5% around 300, and to about 49.5% at the largest value. MEND is a brown solid line with diamond markers, moving from about 44.5% to about 49% near 30, to about 54% around 300, and to about 56.5% at the largest value. MEMIT is a purple solid line with hexagon markers, increasing from about 44% to about 51% near 30, to about 53% around 300, and to about 55% at the largest value. ROME is a green solid line with square markers, rising from about 51% to about 57% near 30, to about 62% around 300, and to about 66% at the largest value.
